text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed autoscaler flipped a GPU nodepool to 0 overnight in eu-west-1 and we had ~30 pods pending with eviction notices this morning. Can someone take a look? :warning:
kevin: Ack. Which nodepool?
ash: looks like gpu-prod-eu-west-1-spot. Terraform shows desired 0 in the last apply.
priya: GitOps pipeline shows a helm release rollout at 03:12 that changed HPA minReplicas from 1 -> 0 (chart values override). Possibly why.
maria: Exact — HPA change came from chart values in infra-apps repo. But there was also a recent policy gate that marked "no-on-demand" for that pool so Karpenter/cluster-autoscaler fell back to spot; combined with min=0 it scaled to 0.
kevin: Do we have logs from the GitOps operator? Maybe the apply failed partially and then retried leading to inconsistent state between controller and cluster.
insights-bot: [alert] 1923456789: GPU nodepool gpu-prod-eu-west-1-spot scaled from 2 -> 0 between 03:15 and 03:18. 27 pods pending (gpu=true). Pod eviction rate increased 03:20.
ash: kubectl get hpa -n ml-serving gpu-inference-hpa -o yaml

```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: gpu-inference-hpa
spec:
  minReplicas: 0
  maxReplicas: 12
  metrics: ...
```

priya: There's also a Helm values file in infra-apps/aws/eu-west-1/values.yaml with `hpa.minReplicas: 0` — was that intended? I thought we pinned min to 1 for prod inference.
maria: Not intended. I searched PR history — a chart override landed yesterday from a branch that was supposed to be staging-only. Looks like env overlay confusion.
kevin: Can we revert the values override and force a hotfix? Helm diff in GitOps shows the change came from commit a7f3b2.
ash: I'll open a rollback PR to set minReplicas: 1 and bump chart. We should also patch running HPA to 1 to un-pend pods while we wait for nodepool to come back.
priya: FYI the GitOps apply failed to create the associated nodepool resource because the Terraform module in infra-account had a policy check that rejected on-demand nodepool creation due to budget tag mismatch. That prevented Karpenter from getting capacity.
kevin: Ugh — so two things: values/helm caused HPA -> 0, and Terraform policy prevented node creation.
sam: Short-term mitigation: patch HPA to minReplicas:1 and mark remaining gpu pods with toleration to allow scheduling on existing nodes? But we only have spot nodes, they might be insufficient.
maria: Patch HPA now and manually scale nodepool to 2 on eu-west-1 (on-demand) as emergency. I'll trigger manual resize in cloud console.
insights-bot: [action] Created incident: INC-2026-gpu-eviction-warning, owner: eng-infra, priority: P2.
priya: Postmortem items: 1) Prevent staging-only chart overrides from reaching prod overlays (ci gate). 2) Add Terraform policy exception flow to avoid silent rejection blocking autoscaling. 3) Add a linter that flags hpa.minReplicas: 0 for inference workloads.
kevin: Also let's add an automated check in the GitOps pipeline: if a change reduces minReplicas for any HPA tagged prod=true, block and require approval.
nash: For immediate fix I'm applying `kubectl patch hpa gpu-inference-hpa -n ml-serving -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":1}}'` and opening PR to revert values. Will update here when done.
maria: Thanks. After manual nodepool up we should monitor tail latency — those queued requests might have SLO impact.
sam: Cost note — bumping to on-demand overnight will increase spend ~3-4k/day for eu-west, but better than customer impact. We can use short reserved window and then switch back to mixed spot once stable.
priya: Agreed. Also add a policy that prevents HPA minReplicas=0 for gpu-serving workloads in the OPA gate.
kevin: Tracking: revert PR + terraform exception + OPA rule + pipeline approval. Assign owners?
maria: Assigning: revert PR = nash, terraform exception = kevin, OPA rule = priya, pipeline approval = sam. I'll keep incident open until all pods scheduled and latency normal. :white_check_mark:
